name: file-access-guard-coverage-anchoring
body:
source: spec-review feedback-1 (`agent-read-guard-prose/feedback-1`) — the branch-added `solution.component.file-access-guard-prose` is covered by `implemented-by apg.main` + `apg.install_suite`, and the requirement spine also reaches the PRE-EXISTING `solution.container.agent-install` (`apg.cmd_init` + `apg.install_suite`) through `domain.entity.agent-prose` / `domain.entity.permission-grant`. Under the branch's spine-scoped coverage gate, a plan Satisfying `read-guard-prose` or any of its children must carry a task whose target equals each reached solution node's `implemented-by` FQN — but the change is markdown-only, so no task truly modifies `apg.main`, `apg.install_suite`, or `apg.cmd_init`; `solution.note.reconcile-system-anchor` had already rejected a fake `modify apg.main` task as "nonsense".

resolution [with user] — anchor-and-claim the install path. The `.md` prompt templates are not scanned code (embedded via `include_str!` and delivered by `apg.install_suite`), so their coverage anchors to the embedding/delivery Rust. The component body now states plainly that this is a markdown-only, no-Rust-behavior-change delta, and that `apg.main` / `apg.install_suite` are embedding/delivery anchors (per `solution.note.embedded-template-anchor` / `solution.note.markdown-anchoring`); the plan carries a delivery task with `modifies apg.install_suite` as that anchor. `solution.container.agent-install`'s anchors (`apg.cmd_init`, `apg.install_suite`) are the pre-existing `apg init` install/delivery path and are claimed on the same delivery-anchor basis, so the coverage reach is intentional and explained. No fake behavior change is claimed.
